title: Solomon's Prayer of Dedication
overview: 2 Chronicles 6 records Solomon's prayer of dedication for the newly built temple in Jerusalem. This chapter highlights Solomon's acknowledgment of God's promise to David, the significance of the temple as God's dwelling place, and the conditions for God's continued blessing on Israel. Solomon prays for God's presence, forgiveness, and justice, emphasizing the importance of repentance and obedience. The chapter also extends God's covenantal blessings to foreigners who come to worship, underscoring the temple's role as a center for God's name and glory. This prayer sets the theological foundation for Israel's worship and relationship with God in the temple era, affirming God's faithfulness and the people's responsibility.
structure:
**Verses 1-11: Solomon's Address and Historical Reflection.** Solomon begins by recalling God's promise to dwell in thick darkness and contrasts it with the temple he has built as a permanent dwelling place for God. He recounts God's choice of Jerusalem and David, affirming that although David desired to build the temple, it was Solomon who fulfilled this divine plan.

**Verses 12-18: Solomon's Prayer for God's Presence and Faithfulness.** Standing on a bronze platform, Solomon prays before the congregation, praising God's uniqueness and faithfulness to David's covenant. He acknowledges God's transcendence and petitions for His attentive presence in the temple.

**Verses 19-31: Conditions for God's Hearing and Forgiveness.** Solomon outlines specific circumstances under which God will hear prayers made toward the temple, including confession of sin, justice in disputes, and national repentance. He emphasizes God's justice and mercy in responding to His people.

**Verses 32-39: Inclusion of Foreigners and Exiles.** Solomon extends the prayer to include strangers and exiles who come to worship, highlighting the temple's universal significance and God's mercy beyond Israel.

**Verses 40-42: Final Petition and Blessing.** Solomon concludes by asking God to hear the prayers made in the temple, to arise to His resting place, clothe His priests with salvation, and remember the mercies promised to David.

keyVerses.text: And said, O LORD God of Israel, there is no God like thee in the heaven, nor in the earth; which keepest covenant, and shewest mercy unto thy servants, that walk before thee with all their hearts:
keyVerses.significance: This verse emphasizes God's uniqueness and faithfulness to His covenant, highlighting His mercy toward those who sincerely seek Him. It sets the tone for Solomon's prayer, affirming God's character as the foundation of Israel's worship.

keyVerses.text: But will God in very deed dwell with men on the earth? behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house which I have built!
keyVerses.significance: Solomon acknowledges God's transcendence and the mystery of His presence dwelling among men. This verse reflects the tension between God's infinite majesty and His gracious choice to dwell in the temple.

keyVerses.text: When the heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; yet if they pray toward this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou dost afflict them;
keyVerses.significance: This verse underscores the conditional nature of God's blessings, linking repentance and prayer to divine forgiveness and restoration. It highlights the temple as a focal point for seeking God's mercy.

keyVerses.text: Moreover concerning the stranger, which is not of thy people Israel, but is come from a far country for thy great name's sake, and thy mighty hand, and thy stretched out arm; if they come and pray in this house;
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals the inclusive scope of God's mercy, extending beyond Israel to foreigners who seek Him. It affirms the temple's role as a house of prayer for all nations.

keyVerses.text: Now therefore arise, O LORD God, into thy resting place, thou, and the ark of thy strength: let thy priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and let thy saints rejoice in goodness.
keyVerses.significance: Solomon's concluding petition calls for God's manifested presence and blessing upon His people, symbolized by the ark and the priests. It encapsulates the hope for divine favor and joy in God's salvation.

characters.name: Solomon
characters.description: The king of Israel who built the temple in Jerusalem. In this chapter, Solomon leads the dedication prayer, acknowledging God's promises to David and petitioning for God's presence, forgiveness, and justice. His role is pivotal as the fulfiller of God's plan to establish a permanent dwelling for His name.

characters.name: David
characters.description: Solomon's father and the previous king of Israel. Though he desired to build the temple, God chose Solomon to do so. David is significant as the recipient of God's covenant promises, which Solomon references to affirm God's faithfulness.

characters.name: The LORD God of Israel
characters.description: The sovereign God who promises to dwell with His people. He is the recipient of Solomon's prayer and the one who fulfills His covenant with David. God's transcendence and immanence are central themes in this chapter.

themes.description: The chapter focuses on God's dwelling among His people through the temple, balancing His transcendence with His immanence. Solomon prays for God's attentive presence in the temple, which symbolizes God's covenant relationship with Israel.

Solomon recalls God's promises to David, emphasizing that God's actions in building the temple fulfill His covenant. The chapter highlights God's unchanging faithfulness and the conditions for Israel's continued blessing.
The prayer outlines specific circumstances for God's hearing, especially confession and turning from sin. It underscores the necessity of sincere repentance and obedience for receiving God's mercy.
The inclusion of foreigners and exiles in Solomon's prayer points to the temple's role as a house of prayer for all nations, anticipating the broader mission of God beyond Israel.

historicalContext: This chapter is set during the reign of Solomon, circa 970-931 BC, in ancient Israel. The temple was constructed in Jerusalem, the political and religious center chosen by God. Building the temple was a significant national and religious event, symbolizing God's covenant presence with Israel. The cultural context includes the ancient Near Eastern practice of dedicating temples with prayers and sacrifices. Politically, Solomon's reign represented a period of peace and prosperity, allowing for such grand religious projects. The temple served as a unifying symbol for the tribes of Israel and a focal point for worship and national identity.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes God's sovereign covenant faithfulness as demonstrated in Solomon's prayer. The temple is seen as a type pointing to Christ, the true dwelling place of God among men. The conditions of prayer and repentance highlight the necessity of grace and obedience.

Dispensationalists view this chapter as part of the Old Testament temple worship system, which will be fulfilled in the millennial kingdom. Solomon's prayer is understood as addressing national Israel, with a future literal fulfillment of God's promises to David and the temple.

Early Church Fathers often interpreted Solomon's temple and prayer typologically, seeing Christ as the true temple where God dwells. They emphasized the spiritual fulfillment of the temple's promises and the call to prayer and repentance as central to Christian life.

crossReferences.connection: Parallel account of Solomon's dedication prayer, providing additional details and confirming the themes of God's presence and covenant faithfulness.
Speaks of God's choice of Zion as His dwelling place, reinforcing the theological significance of Jerusalem and the temple in 2 Chronicles 6.
Highlights God's transcendence and the importance of a humble, contrite heart over physical temple buildings, complementing Solomon's acknowledgment of God's greatness.
Warns against empty temple worship, underscoring the need for sincere repentance and obedience as Solomon prays for in this chapter.
Jesus quotes Scripture about the temple being a house of prayer, echoing Solomon's prayer and emphasizing the temple's purpose.
Describes Christ as the true high priest and mediator of a new covenant, fulfilling the temple's role Solomon prayed about.

application: Recognize God's faithfulness to His promises and trust Him to fulfill His word in your life.
Approach God with sincere prayer and repentance, acknowledging His holiness and mercy.
Understand the importance of God's presence in your life as the true dwelling place.
Include others in your prayers, remembering God's desire for all nations to know Him.
Commit to walking in obedience to God's law as a condition for His blessing.
Seek to be a house of prayer in your community, reflecting the temple's purpose.
conclusion: 2 Chronicles 6 reveals the heart of Solomon's dedication prayer, emphasizing God's covenant faithfulness, the temple as His dwelling place, and the conditions for divine blessing. It challenges believers to approach God with reverence, repentance, and obedience while embracing the inclusive nature of worship. This chapter remains a profound reminder of God's presence among His people and the power of prayer, encouraging Christians today to cultivate a vibrant relationship with God grounded in His promises and mercy.
timeline: c. 970-931 BC - Reign of Solomon and construction of the First Temple
